worried.definition: Form of worry (participle past): To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.

worse.definition: Form of bad (comparative): Of low quality.

worship.definition: To reverence (a deity, etc.) with supreme respect and veneration; to perform religious exercises in honour of.

worshipped.definition: Form of worship (UK participle past): To reverence (a deity, etc.) with supreme respect and veneration; to perform religious exercises in honour of.

worshipping.definition: Form of worship (UK gerund participle present): To reverence (a deity, etc.) with supreme respect and veneration; to perform religious exercises in honour of.

worthless.definition: Having no worth or use; without value.

would.definition: Past tense of will; usually followed by a bare infinitive.

wouldst.definition: Form of will (archaic indicative past second-person singular): Used to express the future tense, sometimes with an implication of volition or determination when used in the first person. Compare shall.

wound.definition: Form of wind (participle past): To blow air through a wind instrument or horn to make a sound.

wounded.definition: Form of wound (participle past): To hurt or injure (someone) by cutting, piercing, or tearing the skin.

wounds.definition: Form of wound (plural): An injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear, to a (usually external) part of the body.

wove.definition: Form of weave (past): To form something by passing lengths or strands of material over and under one another.

woven.definition: Form of weave (participle past): To form something by passing lengths or strands of material over and under one another.

wrangling.definition: Form of wrangle (gerund participle present): To convince or influence (someone) by arguing or contending.

wrath.definition: Great anger; (countable) an instance of this.

wreaths.definition: Form of wreath (plural): Something twisted, intertwined, or curled.

wreck.definition: Something or someone that has been ruined.

wrecked.definition: Form of wreck (participle past): To destroy violently; to cause severe damage to something, to a point where it no longer works, or is useless.

wrecker.definition: A person or company that dismantles old or wrecked vehicles or other items, to reclaim useful parts.

wrecking.definition: The act by which something is wrecked.

wretched.definition: Characterized by or feeling deep affliction or distress; very miserable.

wretchedness.definition: An unhappy state of mental or physical suffering.

wriggling.definition: Form of wriggle (gerund participle present): To twist one's body to and fro with short, writhing motions; to squirm.

wrinkled.definition: Form of wrinkle (participle past): To make wrinkles in; to cause to have wrinkles.

wrist.definition: The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.

write.definition: To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

writers.definition: Form of writer (plural): A person who writes, or produces literary work; an author can refer to themselves as "the writer".

writes.definition: Form of write (indicative present singular third-person): To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

writing.definition: Form of write (gerund participle present): To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

written.definition: Form of write (participle past): To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

wronged.definition: Form of wrong (participle past): To treat unjustly; to injure or harm; to do wrong by.

wrongs.definition: Form of wrong (plural): Something that is immoral or not good.

wrote.definition: Form of write (past): To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

wrought.definition: Form of work (archaic participle past rare): To do a specific task by employing physical or mental powers.

wry.definition: Turned away, contorted (of the face or body).

yahoos.definition: Form of yahoo (plural): A rough, coarse, loud or uncouth individual.

yard.definition: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.

yards.definition: Form of yard (plural): A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.

ye.definition: The Cyrillic letter Е, е, featured in various Slavic and Turkic languages.

year.definition: Form of here (pronunciation-spelling): This place; this location.

years.definition: Form of year (plural): A period of time akin to the time taken for the Earth to undergo a full cycle of seasons.

yell.definition: To shout; holler; make a loud sound with the voice, especially to express intense emotions such as anger or excitement.

yeomanry.definition: A class of small freeholders who cultivated their own land.

yeomans.definition: An official providing honorable service in a royal or high noble household, ranking between a squire and a page. Especially, a yeoman of the guard, a member of a ceremonial bodyguard to the UK monarch (not to be confused.

yes.definition: An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.

yesterday.definition: The day immediately before today; one day ago.

yet.definition: Thus far; up to the present; up to some unspecified time.

yield.definition: To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

yielded.definition: Form of yield (participle past): To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

yoke.definition: Form of yolk (misspelling): The yellow, spherical part of an egg that is surrounded by the white albumen, and serves as nutriment for the growing young.

yokel.definition: A person from or living in the countryside, viewed as being unsophisticated or naive.

yokels.definition: Form of yokel (plural): A person from or living in the countryside, viewed as being unsophisticated or naive.

yonder.definition: At or in a distant but indicated place.

york.definition: To bowl a yorker at a batsman, especially to get a batsman out in this way.

you.definition: To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).

young.definition: Offspring, especially the immature offspring of animals.

youth.definition: The quality or state of being young.

youths.definition: Form of youth (plural): The quality or state of being young.

zag.definition: One of a series of sharp turns or reversals.

zeal.definition: The fervour or tireless devotion for a person, cause, or ideal and determination in its furtherance; diligent enthusiasm; powerful interest.

zealous.definition: Full of zeal; ardent, fervent; exhibiting enthusiasm or strong passion, particularly in matters of religion.

zenith.definition: The point in the sky vertically above a given position or observer; the point in the celestial sphere opposite the nadir.

zest.definition: The outer skin of a citrus fruit, used as a flavouring or garnish.

zig.definition: Form of zig: A sudden or sharp turn or change of direction.

zig-zag.definition: Form of zigzag (alternative): Moving in, or having a zigzag.
